misconception_description: Student believes that multiple mutually exclusive conditions in a control flow construct must each be written as separate if statements.

solutions.generated_code:
program HitungPasanganTidakSama
kamus
  a, b, c, jumlah : integer
algoritma
  input(a, b, c)
  jumlah <- 0
  if a > b then
    jumlah <- jumlah + 1
  endif
  if a < b then
    jumlah <- jumlah + 1
  endif
  if a == b then
    jumlah <- jumlah + 0
  endif
  if a > c then
    jumlah <- jumlah + 1
  endif
  if a < c then
    jumlah <- jumlah + 1
  endif
  if a == c then
    jumlah <- jumlah + 0
  endif
  if b > c then
    jumlah <- jumlah + 1
  endif
  if b < c then
    jumlah <- jumlah + 1
  endif
  if b == c then
    jumlah <- jumlah + 0
  endif
  output(jumlah)
endprogram

metadata.modification_notes: The student rewrites the single condition (arr[i] != arr[j]) into three separate mutually exclusive conditions: greater than, less than, and equal. Following their misconception that mutually exclusive conditions must be written as separate if statements, they use three consecutive if statements instead of if-elif-elif. The student counts pairs where arr[i] > arr[j] or arr[i] < arr[j] (which covers all unequal pairs) and explicitly doesn't count when arr[i] == arr[j]. While stylistically poor (should use elif), the code works correctly because these conditions are truly mutually exclusive - only one can ever be true at a time. The student believes this is the proper way to handle mutually exclusive cases and thinks their solution correctly solves the problem.
